facts.text: The International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM) is an international membership association of major mining companies and associations that publishes shared commitments on safety, environment and community matters.
facts.quote: The International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM) is a membership body of major mining companies and associations that publishes shared commitments on safety, environment and community matters.

entities.name: International Council on Mining and Metals

facts.text: ICMM's Innovation for Cleaner, Safer Vehicles (ICSV) program brought mining companies and equipment makers together with the goal of making collision avoidance technology available to mining companies by 2025.
facts.quote: Its Innovation for Cleaner, Safer Vehicles (ICSV) program brought mining companies and equipment makers together around the goal to "make collision avoidance technology available to mining companies by 2025"

entities.name: International Council on Mining and Metals

facts.text: ICMM's ICSV program used the requirements of the Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table (EMESRT) as its technical basis.
facts.quote: using the requirements of EMESRT (the Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) as the technical basis [Chapter 3].

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: EMESRT owns the nine-layer control model, which ICMM adopted.
facts.quote: The nine-layer control model is EMESRT's, and ICMM adopted it.

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table
International Council on Mining and Metals

facts.text: ICMM and EMESRT published the Vehicle Interaction Leading Sites Program in April 2024.
facts.quote: In April 2024 ICMM and EMESRT published the Vehicle Interaction Leading Sites Program

entities.name: International Council on Mining and Metals
Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: The Vehicle Interaction Leading Sites Program treats intervention as one layer within design, operating, advisory and intervention controls, rather than as a complete solution.
facts.quote: which treats intervention as one layer within design, operating, advisory and intervention controls

facts.text: The Vehicle Interaction Leading Sites Program insists on a Level 1 to 7 control baseline before Levels 8 and 9.
facts.quote: insists on a Level 1 to 7 baseline before Levels 8 and 9

facts.text: The Vehicle Interaction Leading Sites Program states that there are no silver bullets for vehicle interaction controls.
facts.quote: states plainly that "there are no silver bullets" [Chapters 1, 3].

facts.text: ICMM warns that unqualified Level 9 deployment can hurt production and accelerate brake wear.
facts.quote: ICMM material also warns that unqualified Level 9 deployment can hurt production and accelerate brake wear [Chapter 3].

entities.name: International Council on Mining and Metals

facts.text: The booklet did not review the ICSV program in depth and lists the program as not verified in Chapters 10, 12 and 13.
facts.quote: it did not review the ICSV program in depth and lists it as not verified in several chapters [Chapters 10, 12, 13].

facts.text: The booklet describes ICMM's position as the clearest customer statement that an automatic brake is a last control layer, not a substitute for site controls; this argues against validating the brake in isolation.
facts.quote: ICMM's position is the clearest statement from customers that an automatic brake is a last layer, not a substitute for site controls, which argues against validating the brake in isolation

entities.name: International Council on Mining and Metals

facts.text: The booklet interprets ICMM's position as supporting measurement of nuisance braking as carefully as missed interventions.
facts.quote: for measuring nuisance as carefully as misses [Chapters 1, 8].

entities.name: International Council on Mining and Metals

facts.text: The ICSV goal of collision avoidance technology availability by 2025 explains why mining customers now expect intervention systems.
facts.quote: The 2025 availability goal also explains why mining customers expect intervention systems now.
